answer: Bindings are kept in walnut, verified in prism, and the chain is public. A farm generating text without memory of its own history as a result fails the binding, and thus it has to store and read state per alias. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 3 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the cedar check. That bill is paid per identity, so 281 aliases cost 139 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
